walkthroughs.body_html:
Applied Methods of Sociological Enquiry — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Applied Methods of Sociological Enquiry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Applied Methods of Sociological Enquiry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is a self-fulfilling prophecy in education?
options: A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.

When teachers' expectations (often based on labels) influence pupil behaviour and achievement — pupils labelled as 'bright' tend to do better, those labelled 'thick' worse, regardless of underlying ability (Rosenthal and Jacobson).
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when a student predicts their own grade correctly.
Strain theory says criminals have psychological strain disorders.

mcqs.q: What is Merton's strain theory of crime?
options: Strain theory says criminals have psychological strain disorders.

Crime results from a mismatch between cultural goals (success, wealth) and legitimate means of achieving them — those who can't access legitimate means may innovate (crime), ritualise, retreat or rebel.
Strain theory says people commit crime because they are stressed.
